全球。图片约 1100 万张，购自一家直接与摄影师合作的图片供应商，拍摄年份跨度: Global. About 11 million images, purchased from an image supplier that works directly with photographers, with a wide range of capture years, up to 2022 at the latest. The images carry no geotags, so regions are inferred: the authors used an ELMo named-entity recognition model to extract place names from image captions and then mapped them to countries; the inferred results are not public. By image count: Europe 49.8% (47 countries, 5.4 million images), Asia and Oceania 36.2% (70 countries, 3.9 million), North America 7.7% (4 countries, 830K), Latin America and the Caribbean 3.5% (42 countries, 380K), Africa 2.8% (54 countries, 300K). By income: high-income countries 54.0%, middle-income 45.0%, low-income 0.9%. Most countries have more than 1,000 images each, and the top three countries by image count are on different continents. The share of street-view imagery is not officially reported.

中国（百度采集）。官方 README 称数据'在不同城市、多种交通状况下采集'，: China (collected by Baidu). The official README says the data were 'collected in different cities under various traffic conditions' but does not list the specific cities of the scene-parsing subset. The TPAMI version describes the whole dataset as 'covering 10 cities in China' (introduction) and '4 regions in China' (Table I). Another subset (self-localization) is noted as coming from 6 sites in Beijing, Guangzhou, Chengdu and Shanghai, but it is not the scene-parsing subset. The collection vehicle is a mid-size SUV with a roof-mounted Riegl VMX-1HA mapping system: 2 VUX-1HA laser scanners, a VMX-CS6 camera system (two forward-facing cameras, 3384×2710) and an IMU/GNSS. Vehicle speed is about 30 km/h, and the cameras trigger about every 1 metre. Conditions: Table I records 'various weather, day time'; the main text mentions variation in morning, noon and night illumination and in peak and off-peak hours. The CVPRW version shows scenes with strong shadows or glare, overpass shadows and car-body reflections, and lists snow and fog as future plans. The data are divided into easy/moderate/hard by complexity (density of traffic participants). The collection year is not stated; the first scene-parsing data were released on 2018-03-08.

印度班加罗尔、海得拉巴两市及其郊区。路况包括城市和乡村、高速公路、单车道和双车道: Bengaluru and Hyderabad in India, and their suburbs. Road types include urban and rural roads, highways, and single-lane and two-lane roads. Road conditions are highly unstructured: rapid urban expansion, a lot of roadside construction, unclear road boundaries, frequent pedestrian crossings, and high densities of motorcycles and trucks. Images are taken from one camera of a vehicle-mounted forward-facing stereo pair (the paper states the cameras are calibrated and undistorted); the official site says 'front-facing camera mounted on a car'. There are 182 driving sequences; frames were extracted from the videos at varying rates, more densely in crowded places such as intersections, and 10,004 frames were annotated in total. Lighting includes noon, dawn and dusk; some images have heavy shadows (the paper says this is common in the long summer), dense cloudy skies, and appearance changes caused by particulates such as fog, dust and haze. The paper does not mention night. The collection years, vehicle model and camera model are not disclosed (the arXiv version of the paper was released in November 2018).
